title: Private deploy onboarding & key-escrow PRD: RBAC tiers, SAML SSO flow, HSM/KMS integration and audit retention
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Clarify and lock scope for Private Deployment onboarding related to identity, keying, and audit controls. This PRD captures the final requirements, open trade-offs, scope changes since initial draft, and concrete acceptance criteria for sign-off by PM, Security, Engineering, and Legal.

Context: Several enterprise customers require a hardened onboarding flow for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments that includes: (1) SAML SSO integration with IdP provisioning patterns, (2) RBAC tiering that maps to their internal roles and least privilege, (3) KMS/HSM options supporting both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key with optional escrow), and (4) audit log retention & export controls suitable for SOC2/ISO evidence. Earlier drafts assumed a single customer-managed KMS option; customer feedback and Security review require an HSM-backed escrow path for some regulated customers.

Scope (final):
- Mandatory: SAML 2.0 SP integration with IdP-initiated and IdP provisioning hints, metadata exchange, and SAML attribute mapping for group/role sync.
- Mandatory: RBAC model with three baseline tiers (Viewer, Operator, Admin) and a mapping guide for custom role names. Enforce least-privilege defaults for private deployments.
- Mandatory: Audit logs: immutable delivery to customer-specified log sinks (S3/GCS/EventHub) and retention policy control (30/90/365 days). Provide signed audit manifest for export.
- Optional (customer-configurable): KMS modes: Redwood-managed KMS, Customer-managed KMS (external cloud KMS integration), and HSM-backed key escrow (for on-prem air-gapped environments, escrow held in a FIPS-140-2/HSM appliance hosted by customer or validated partner).
- Excluded: Full key rotation automation across all partner HSMs in initial launch (will be follow-up).

Scope changes and rationale:
- Change: Added HSM-backed escrow option after SG review (2026-02-16). Rationale: several regulated customers required hardware-backed custody with verifiable attestations; this increases initial engineering cost but reduces legal blockers for those customers.
- Change: Reduced default audit retention choices from open-ended to three buckets (30/90/365) to simplify compliance sign-off and reduce storage cost surface.

Open trade-offs and decisions:
- Key custody model: trade between simplest UX (Redwood-managed) vs compliance (customer custody). Decision: ship with both Redwood-managed and Customer-managed KMS on day-1; HSM escrow as gated feature for regulated customers after attestation checks.
- RBAC enforcement surface: enforce at API layer vs. at control plane. Decision: enforce at control plane with per-route tokens for critical operations; runtime enforcement to be handled by ENG as part of dedicated capacity auth.

Non-functional constraints:
- SAML assertion processing latency must not increase API auth path by >30ms P50.
- Audit log delivery SLA: 99.9% daily delivery success for scheduled exports.
- HSM integrations must meet FIPS-140-2 validation and provide CSR/attestation artifacts for legal.

Acceptance criteria (detailed):
- SAML: SP metadata exchange and a successful end-to-end IdP-initiated login test with attribute-based role mapping (test vector included).
- RBAC: Role assignment UI/API and enforcement tests demonstrating least-privilege for Operator role against a set of 12 blocked actions.
- KMS: Successful provisioning of a customer-managed KMS key (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) and crypto operations (encrypt/decrypt) using that key for a sample tenant.
- HSM escrow: Proof-of-concept integration documented with one validated HSM vendor, including attestation fetch and a disaster-recovery key-unwrap test.
- Audit logs: Export of immutable logs to S3 with retention policy enforcement and signed manifest generation; verify integrity via SHA256 checks.

RBAC baseline roles created in console; Operator role blocked from create/delete cluster actions in tests
Customer-managed KMS key integrated and used for at-rest encryption verification for a tenant
HSM escrow integration documented with successful attestation retrieval and key unwrap DR test
